newsitem.title: UK: EMS/ERM fever grips FX market, lira and markka star.
newsitem.headline: EMS/ERM fever grips FX market, lira and markka star.

text.p: Exchange rate mechanism fever has gripped the European forex market with traders buying Italian lira and Finnish markka amid speculation of their imminent ERM entry.
Since the beginning of last month the lira has rallied around 3.4 percent to a two-year high while the Finnish markka has risen nearly two percent to a 10-month high.

A lot of this represents convergence trades as the economic backdrop improves sufficiently to qualify for European monetary union (EMU) but thoughts of near-term ERM entry, another qualification for EMU, provides a definite boost.
"What do you do, go home short or go home long of a high yielding currency that might go up over the weekend if they enter?" said one trader on Friday. "Where's your risk return on that?"
Apart from many in the market gussing that central rates will be pegged above current levels, currencies also get a boost from ERM entry as devaluation risk is perceived to be removed.

So both the lira and markka are likely to remain firm, particularly ahead of weekends, as traders bet on the timing of entry. Any ERM announcement will be made out of normal market hours and most likely over the weekend.
And the excitement is likely to build as the end of the year approaches because both Italy and Finland are determined to be in the EMU A-team in January 1, 1999.
One of the Maastricht pre-requisites is participation in the ERM, respecting the normal bands, for at least two years without devaluing.

"It think both Italy and Finland will go into the ERM before the end of the end of the year," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International. "The Italians can only control their destiny to some extent, budget is one thing and re-entering the ERM is the other."

"It will not be long before Italy is in the ERM again," Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said in an interview for Reuters Financial Television in Naples, where he is among ministers attending an Italian-French summit.

The lira was ejected from the ERM, along with sterling, in September 1992, and while there is no precedent for a country to re-enter it is likely the procedure for new entrants will be adopted, said Joe Prendergast, FX strategist at Merrill Lynch.

"The final approval of any central rate will be subject to approval by the ECOFIN council, while the initial pre-entry negotiations will have been taking place within the EU monetary committee and the European Monetary Institute," he said.
Traders seem to be looking at a central rate of between 950 and 1,000 for mark/lira and just below 3.0 for mark/markka, which compares with current levels of 993.50 and 2.9850.
Meanwhile, the market rumour-mill will continue to grind with wild talk circulating this week -- which analysts described as preposterous -- that sterling was about to re-enter the ERM.

This was based on the unlikely theory that as sterling entered the ERM in October 1990 between the opposition Labour and ruling Conservative party annual conferences it would go in this weekend, between this year's party conferences.
"Even if Italy and Finland do go in it won't put pressure on the UK," Lyons said. "It's just impossible to tie up all the legislation to go in soon."

But traders are expecting the lira and the markka to go in anytime soon. "All the Italian and Finnish analysts will be going out for nice haircuts this weekend in case they go in and television stations start ringing up," said one trader.
